title: Unfolding a box
_map: Unfolding a box (stretch). Big idea: a flat net folds into a 3D shape. Creative: find different flat shapes that fold into a cube (there are 11).
_story: The robot wants a box for its eggs. It unfolds a cube into a flat cross of 6 squares, then folds it back. There are 11 different nets; Ismaeel hunts for some with paper.
_stepChain: a cube has 6 square faces (faces-edges-corners) → cut along some edges and lay it flat → a flat shape that folds into a solid is called a net → fold it back → not every 6-square shape works → there are 11 cube nets

talk.goodAnswer: a flat shape that folds up into a 3D shape, like the cross of 6 squares that makes a cube.

talk.ask: Does every shape made of 6 squares fold into a cube?
talk.goodAnswer: no; only 11 of them do. Some overlap or leave a gap.

handsOn: Draw a cross of 6 squares on paper, cut it out, and fold it into a cube. Then try to invent a different net that also works. There are 11 to find!

narration.speaker: robot
narration.text: I need a box for my eggs. Look, here's a cube box. I wonder what it looks like if I unfold it?
Cut along some of the edges, and lay it flat. It's a cross of 6 squares! A flat shape that folds up into a solid shape is called a net.
Now watch it fold back up. Each square folds up to become one face. 6 squares, 6 faces.

narration.speaker: robot
narration.text: Is the cross the only net for a cube? I think there must be hundreds!

question.prompt: How many different nets do you think fold into a cube?
question.reveal: 11! Mathematicians have checked every way. Some shapes made of 6 squares fold perfectly. Others overlap, or leave a hole.

narration.text: Here's a hunt for you. With paper and scissors, find some of the 11 nets. Try a line of 4 squares, with one square on top and one underneath. Does it fold into a cube?

rule.text: A net folds up into a solid shape.
rule.ask: Can you say what a net is? Say it out loud. Then tap the eye.
rule.spoken: A net is a flat shape that folds up into a solid. A cube's net has 6 squares, and there are 11 different ones.

bonus.prompt: Bonus: a net for a pyramid with a square bottom. How many triangles does it need?
bonus.reveal: 4 triangles round one square: they fold up to meet at the top.
